working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is one of the most links-rich counties in the British Isles, but most visitors fly in, play Royal County Down, and leave. This post makes the case for a proper three-course circuit around the county, treating RCD as the headline act but giving Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle the credit they deserve as genuinely distinctive links in their own right.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD), Newcastle, County Down, Northern Ireland. Established 1889. 36 holes: Championship Links (par 71, approx. 7,186 yards, course rating 75.0, slope 142) and Annesley Links (par 66, 4,617 yards). Designed originally by Old Tom Morris; later refined by Harry Vardon and Harry Colt.
- RCD setting: foot of the Mourne Mountains on Dundrum Bay, towering dunes of marram grass, widely regarded as one of the top-ranked courses in the world by major publications.
- RCD visitor access: available Monday, Tuesday, Friday all day; Thursday mornings; Sunday afternoons. No play Wednesdays or Saturdays. Advance booking essential via enquiry form on royalcountydown.org. All play in four-ball groups. Buggies not permitted — walking only. Caddies available.
- RCD green fees (from where2golf): Annesley Links high season approx. £60 per round; Championship Links high season weekdays/Sunday pm approx. £325. Note: one source (thewanderinggolfers.com, 2026) quotes Championship at £450 — fees vary by season and source, do not state a single definitive figure in the post; describe as 'premium' and direct readers to royalcountydown.org.
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole clifftop links, Castle Place, Ardglass, Co. Down BT30 7TP. Founded 1896. Par 70, approx. 6,216 yards. Set on cliffs above the Irish Sea; Irish Sea comes into play on eight holes. Clubhouse occupies part of a fortified building with initial construction dating to 1405 — claimed by members to be the oldest golf clubhouse in the world (rival claimants exist). Visitors welcome; more restricted at weekends; advance booking required; handicap required. High season green fees quoted variously at £115 weekday / £135 weekend (where2golf) — treat as approximate, may have changed; direct readers to club website ardglassgolfclub.com.
- Ardglass setting: opening six holes are the most dramatic, with the par-3 2nd crossing a ravine and other holes separated from the sea by jagged rocks. Sea views present throughout. About 30 minutes from RCD at Newcastle.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: 18-hole links, 142 Main Road, Cloughey, Ards Peninsula, County Down BT22 1JA. Founded 1902. Current course layout designed by James Braid in 1934. Par 69/70 (sources vary slightly), approx. 6,167 yards. The most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland. Nearest true links course to Belfast (approx. 45 minutes via A20 through Newtownards). Quick-draining links terrain means course rarely closed even after heavy rain. Visitors welcome 7 days per week. Green fees approx. £35 weekday / £40 weekend (Golfshake). Signature hole: par-4 10th, 435 yards, reputedly one of the most difficult par 4s in Irish golf.
- Getting there from mainland UK: Belfast has two airports (George Best Belfast City, BHD; Belfast International, BFS). BHD is 30-40 minutes from Newcastle/Downpatrick by car. Ferry routes: Cairnryan (Scotland) to Belfast via Stena Line (approx. 2 hrs 15 min); Cairnryan to Larne via P&O (approx. 2 hrs); Liverpool Birkenhead to Belfast via Stena Line (approx. 8 hrs, overnight option available). Driving from Belfast to Newcastle (RCD) approx. 45 min via A24. Driving from Belfast to Kirkistown Castle approx. 45 min via A20.
- Logical circuit itinerary: Day 1 Kirkistown Castle (closest true links to Belfast, good warm-up, modest green fee), Day 2 Ardglass (clifftop drama, mid-range fee), Day 3 RCD Championship (headline round). Annesley Links at RCD is a strong add-on for a fourth day or as a second round.
- Accommodation: Slieve Donard Hotel in Newcastle is the obvious base (adjacent to RCD); Burrendale Hotel Newcastle also mentioned as four-star option for County Down trips.
must_avoid:
- Do not fabricate or state a single definitive green fee for Royal County Down — sources conflict and fees change seasonally. Describe as premium and direct readers to the official site.
- Do not invent quotes attributed to pros, reviewers, or real people.
- No affiliate links unless the operator/hotel is in /src/content/approved-partners.md; if not listed, mention informationally only with no link and no explanatory note to the reader.
- No gambling, betting, health/injury advice, or financial advice content.
- No em dashes anywhere in the post.
- No invented personal anecdotes (the site owner has not necessarily played these courses).
- Do not duplicate the southwest-ireland-golf-circuit post angle; this post is focused on County Down, Northern Ireland, not the Republic.
- The Ardglass 'oldest clubhouse' claim should be noted as the club's own claim, with the caveat that rival claimants exist — do not state it as settled fact.
